Zechariah, Prophecy of
zek-uh-RYE-uh, PROF-uh-see
proper noun
The post-exilic prophetic book of Zechariah; the Hebrew name Zekaryah, “the LORD remembers.”

📖 Biblical Definition

The prophecy of Zechariah is the post-exilic book of the prophet who, with Haggai, stirred the returned remnant to rebuild the temple, and whose visions and oracles are among the most richly messianic in all the Old Testament. Zechariah opens with a call to repentance—turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts—and unfolds in a series of night visions of the LORD’s jealousy for Jerusalem, the cleansing of Joshua the high priest, and the promise of the Branch, the Servant who shall build the temple of the LORD and bear the glory. The later chapters pour out prophecies of the coming King and Shepherd that the Gospels record fulfilled in Christ: the King coming to Zion lowly and riding upon an ass; the thirty pieces of silver, the price at which the Shepherd was valued, cast to the potter; the LORD pierced, on whom they shall look and mourn; the Shepherd smitten and the sheep scattered. The book closes looking to the day when the LORD shall be king over all the earth, and holiness unto the LORD shall be written even upon the bells of the horses. The dictionary reads Zechariah as a fountain of messianic prophecy, the book that, more than almost any other, foretold the humble King, the pierced and smitten Shepherd, and the final reign of the LORD over all the earth.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The post-exilic prophecy of Zechariah; visions of the LORD’s jealousy for Jerusalem and a fountain of messianic prophecy—the humble King, the smitten Shepherd, the pierced LORD.

ZECHARIAH, PROPHECY OF, the post-exilic prophet who urged the temple’s rebuilding.

Opens with a call to repentance and night visions of the LORD’s jealousy for Zion.

Promises the Branch who shall build the temple and bear the glory.

Foretells the King coming lowly, riding upon an ass (Zec 9:9).

Foretells the thirty pieces of silver, the pierced LORD, and the smitten Shepherd.

📖 Key Scripture

Zec 9:9 — "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass."

Zec 11:12 — "And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver."

Zec 12:10 — "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn."

Zec 13:7 — "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though critical readers deny the unity of the book and the predictive force of its messianic prophecies; the Gospels confess them fulfilled in Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The matter to answer is the critical denial that touches the book: the division of Zechariah into an authentic first part and a later “Deutero-Zechariah,” and the refusal of genuine predictive prophecy, so that the uncanny correspondences with the life of Christ are explained away as vague poetry or after-the-fact reading. The dictionary holds the unity and the predictive power of the book. The Gospels themselves cite these very texts as fulfilled: the King on the ass at the triumphal entry, the thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter, the pierced One looked upon, the smitten Shepherd and scattered sheep at Gethsemane. This is prophecy, not coincidence.

The principle to recover is the messianic unity of Scripture, with Zechariah a chief witness. The book that urged the rebuilding of the stone temple pointed beyond it to the Branch who would build the true temple and reign as King and Priest; its King comes lowly to Zion, is valued at a slave’s price, is pierced and smitten, and shall yet be king over all the earth. The LORD remembers—the meaning of the prophet’s name—and keeps every word concerning His Christ.
